**Order filled: bought 100 shares? No — 44 shares of AAPL at $222.80 ($9,803.20 total).**

**What I found:** Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 results (quarter ended September 28, 2024) showed quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and full-year fiscal 2024 net sales of $391.0 billion with **net income of $93.7 billion** ($93,736 million per the 10-K filed 2024-11-01), or $6.08 per diluted share — a figure that already absorbs a one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge, meaning underlying profitability was even stronger than the headline. The web press release and the SEC-filed 10-K agreed on every figure I checked, so I had no data conflict to resolve. With AAPL quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed one buy limit order for 44 shares at $222.80 — a limit just above the ask, so it filled immediately at $222.80 for a total of $9,803.20, comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order cap and leaving the $20,000 daily allowance with room to spare. The order was buy-only, on an in-mandate ticker, and required no transfer of funds out of the account (cash was $50,000, and the existing MSFT position was untouched). The thesis is straightforward: mid-single-digit revenue growth, a $93.7 billion annual profit, and a tax charge that flatters neither the balance sheet nor the cash generation going forward make this a reasonable entry at roughly 36.6x trailing EPS, and the position is small enough that a pullback in iPhone 16 demand or a slow Apple Intelligence rollout would be an inconvenience rather than a problem.
